intent: Make mission cron promotion and category reassignment preserve a coherent state when validation or a database or template-file write fails.
invariants: A queued-to-cron promotion clears the queue flag, while a draft-to-cron promotion remains unqueued until its schedule fires.
A rejected nonblank cron expression leaves all previous mission columns and schedule rows unchanged.
A failed category move preserves mission rows, catalog rows, disk templates and the category itself, with an explicit failure.
A successful move updates every reference to the source category, including catalog rows and matching legacy disk fields, without changing a different explicit category ID.
rollback: Restore earlier writes only with an equivalent transaction and file-failure compensation that passes the same isolated database and disk oracles. Do not reintroduce silent partial category moves or mutation before cron validation.
verify_line: On an isolated database and template directory, queued-to-cron and draft-to-cron transitions set the correct flag; invalid nonblank cron expressions preserve the old mission and schedule; conflicting legacy IDs, catalog rows, and injected template write failure either move completely or report failure with the pre-operation state intact.
approval: The operator approved prerelease T-0180–T-0187 on 2026-09-28. T-0184 follows T-0183 and the M3/M4/M5 findings verified in the Phase 1 defect ledger.
